<reason>PRO won by turning CON's central example and holding the key distinctions. CON cited low unemployment through disinflation as proof patience works; PRO showed that is the motion working with anchored expectations, and CON never restored the anchor-without-commitment claim. PRO's level-vs-trend answer to supply shocks and large-recession-avoids-scarring inversion stayed live, while PRO's catch-up contradiction press forced CON into a catch-up-by-attrition concession that PRO framed as drift. CON's concentrated-scarring case was vivid but increasingly repeated.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's R1 turn of the soft landing plus level-vs-trend reply, extended by the Q2 catch-up trap in R2: either no catch-up means 3 years of real pay cuts for the weak, or catch-up means the second round CON denies.</best_rebuttal>
